description: nf-core/rnaseq samplesheet context JSON template aligned to the current nf-core/rnaseq usage documentation and example samplesheet. Designed for LLM-friendly parsing and direct creation of the final pipeline CSV.

pseudo_aligner.help: transcriptome pseudo-aligner. Default salmon is an intentional curated default (matches the lab's standard rnaseq run); the upstream nf-core/rnaseq default is none (null).

gencode.help: set true when the GTF is GENCODE-formatted

save_reference.help: save built genome indices for reuse

save_trimmed.help: save adapter-trimmed FastQ (preserves the prior Luria run.sh default)

pipeline.name: nf-core/rnaseq
pipeline.core_rule: The first 4 columns must be sample, fastq_1, fastq_2, strandedness. Additional columns may follow after these.
pipeline.multi_run_behavior: Rows with the same sample value are treated as multiple runs of the same sample and concatenated before downstream analysis.
pipeline.single_vs_paired_behavior: The pipeline infers whether a library is single-end or paired-end from whether fastq_2 is blank or populated.

validation_rules: First 4 columns must be exactly: sample, fastq_1, fastq_2, strandedness.
The file consumed by the pipeline must be comma-separated (CSV).
sample must be repeated across rows for multiple lanes/runs of the same biological sample.
fastq_1 should be a gzipped FASTQ path ending in .fastq.gz or .fq.gz.
fastq_2 should be blank for single-end libraries and populated for paired-end libraries.
strandedness must be one of: auto, forward, reverse, unstranded.
If seq_platform or seq_center are used, place them after the first 4 columns.
genome_bam, transcriptome_bam, and percent_mapped are optional reprocessing-oriented columns.
Extra custom columns may be appended after the required columns for LLM/human context, but downstream custom handling is your responsibility.
notes: This context file is for LLM-assisted samplesheet creation and validation. The final file supplied to nf-core/rnaseq should be a CSV whose first four columns remain exactly: sample, fastq_1, fastq_2, strandedness.

samplesheet_columns.description: Column-level field dictionary for the nf-core/rnaseq input samplesheet.

sample.description: Custom sample name. Use the same value for multiple sequencing runs/libraries from the same biological sample so nf-core concatenates them before downstream analysis.
sample.validation_hints: Keep stable across lanes/reruns; avoid commas; spaces will be converted to underscores by the pipeline; consider encoding group/replicate with underscores for easier PCA grouping.

fastq_1.description: Full path to read 1 FASTQ file for Illumina short reads.
fastq_1.validation_hints: Must point to gzipped FASTQ; absolute path recommended; for multi-lane resequencing add another row with same sample and a different FASTQ path.

fastq_2.required: required header, value optional for single-end
fastq_2.description: Full path to read 2 FASTQ file for paired-end libraries. Leave blank for single-end libraries.
fastq_2.validation_hints: If paired-end, should contain mate 2 and not be blank; if single-end, keep blank; header must still exist.

strandedness.description: Library strandedness / strand-specificity used by downstream quantification and QC.
strandedness.validation_hints: Use auto when unsure; auto makes the pipeline infer strandedness from a subsample of reads. Use one value consistently per library row.

seq_platform.position_rule: May appear after the first 4 columns
seq_platform.description: Per-sample sequencing platform for BAM read group PL tag.
seq_platform.validation_hints: Use only when platforms vary by sample; otherwise prefer global --seq_platform. For standard short-read RNA-seq this is often ILLUMINA.

seq_center.position_rule: May appear after the first 4 columns
seq_center.description: Per-sample sequencing center for BAM read group CN tag.
seq_center.validation_hints: Use only when centers vary by sample; otherwise prefer global --seq_center.

genome_bam.position_rule: May appear after the first 4 columns
genome_bam.description: Genome-aligned BAM from a prior nf-core/rnaseq run, for the BAM reprocessing workflow.
genome_bam.validation_hints: Use with --skip_alignment; best supported when produced by this same pipeline.

transcriptome_bam.position_rule: May appear after the first 4 columns
transcriptome_bam.description: Transcriptome-aligned BAM from a prior nf-core/rnaseq run, for the BAM reprocessing workflow.
transcriptome_bam.validation_hints: Optional in the BAM reprocessing mode; best supported when produced by this same pipeline.

percent_mapped.position_rule: May appear after the first 4 columns
percent_mapped.description: Percent of reads mapped during alignment, useful in BAM reprocessing / QC contexts.
percent_mapped.validation_hints: Numeric percentage only; no percent sign if you want strict CSV numeric parsing.

report_writer_guidance.purpose: Use this file as the single context specification for constructing an nf-core/rnaseq samplesheet from already-scraped study metadata.
report_writer_guidance.workflow_role: Selected when the upstream agent identifies report_writing mode and chooses NFCORE:RNAseq as the report type.
report_writer_guidance.output_expectation: Populate the samplesheet_template structure and emit a pipeline-ready CSV using the required column order.
population_priority: Assign one logical sample identifier per biological sample or per library, depending on how the study metadata distinguishes runs.
Map read 1 FASTQ files to fastq_1 and read 2 FASTQ files to fastq_2 using file naming or explicit mate metadata.
For single-end data, keep fastq_2 present as a header but leave its value blank.
For multiple lanes or resequenced runs from the same sample, repeat the same sample value across rows and change only the FASTQ paths.
If strandedness is not explicitly known, set strandedness to auto.
Populate optional columns only when the metadata clearly supports them; otherwise leave them blank.
final_checks: Column order starts with: sample, fastq_1, fastq_2, strandedness.
All FASTQ paths are placed in the correct mate column.
Single-end vs paired-end handling is consistent across the file.
Strandedness uses only allowed values: auto, forward, reverse, unstranded.
Optional columns, if included, appear after the first four required columns.
